senses.definition: Energy sent out in waves or particles. Light is a kind of radiation.
senses.example: Radiation from the Sun can travel through empty space.

senses.definition: The distance from the middle of a circle to its edge, or a line showing that distance.
senses.example: A circle with a radius of three centimeters measures six centimeters straight across.

senses.definition: A series of returns that keep a ball or shuttle in play during one point.
senses.example: They sent the ball over the net six times during the rally.

senses.definition: Fast working memory that holds information a computer is using right now.
senses.example: When you restart, the computer can put the apps it needs back into RAM.

senses.definition: To approve a written agreement by following its official rules.
senses.example: Several states had to ratify the new Constitution.

senses.definition: Again, as part of a word for doing something another time.
senses.example: If a robot needs a new coat of paint, you can repaint it.

senses.definition: To work out the meaning of written words or signs, by sight, touch, or another method.
senses.example: We read the trail sign to see how far the pond was.

senses.definition: To say aloud the words that are written down.
senses.example: My brother wanted me to read the poem aloud.

senses.definition: A part of a cell or a nerve that notices a change and helps the body respond to it.
senses.example: A receptor can sense a light touch.

senses.definition: A flat shape with four straight sides and four square corners.
senses.example: A square is a rectangle whose four sides are all the same length.

senses.definition: A cell in the blood that carries oxygen to the body.
senses.example: A red blood cell changes shape to pass through a narrow tube.

senses.definition: A thin piece of cane or another material that moves rapidly to start sound in some instruments.
senses.example: The reed on the clarinet moved when the player blew.

senses.definition: The way light or sound bounces off a surface.
senses.example: I saw my reflection in the still water.

senses.definition: A quick response the body makes without you having to decide first.
senses.example: Pulling away quickly from a sharp point can be a reflex.

senses.definition: The bending of a wave as it enters something where it moves at a different speed.
senses.example: Refraction can make a straw look bent near the surface of a glass of water.

senses.definition: A practice session for a performance, ceremony, or other event.
senses.example: At rehearsal, we practiced walking onto the stage quietly.

senses.definition: A race in which teammates each complete part of the course.
senses.example: We took turns running one lap each in the relay.

senses.definition: Able to be trusted to work well, show up, or give information that is usually right.
senses.example: The accurate weather station gave us a reliable record of the temperature.

senses.definition: The amount left over after you make as many equal groups as you can.
senses.example: After dividing eleven pencils into two equal groups of five, the remainder is one.

senses.definition: A person chosen to speak or act for other people.
senses.example: We chose a class representative to bring our ideas to the school council.

senses.definition: Typical of a larger group or good at showing what that larger group is like.
senses.example: One unusually hot day is not representative of the whole year.

senses.definition: A country where leaders govern on behalf of the public and the head of the country is not a ruler who gets the job by birth.
senses.example: In a republic with elections, people can vote for a president or for other leaders.

senses.definition: A place where water is collected and stored, often behind a dam.
senses.example: The reservoir held rainwater for the dry months.

senses.definition: A part that vibrates along with a sound and can make it stronger. In a hollow resonator the air inside can vibrate, too.
senses.example: The tube below a bar can act as a resonator.

senses.definition: The light-sensitive layer lining the back of the eye.
senses.example: Light lands on the retina and some of its cells send signals.

senses.definition: A way of describing colors by how much red, green, and blue light they use.
senses.example: A screen can combine RGB light to show yellow.

senses.definition: A plant stem that grows sideways, usually under or along the ground.
senses.example: New shoots grew at points on the iris rhizome.

senses.definition: A match or close match between sounds at the ends of words.
senses.example: Bat and hat make a rhyme.

senses.definition: A pattern of sounds, beats, or movements as they happen in time.
senses.example: We clapped the rhythm of the tune without singing it.

senses.definition: Curved bones and nearby cartilage that surround the chest and protect parts inside it.
senses.example: My rib cage moves when I take a deep breath.

senses.definition: To travel on or in a vehicle or on the back of an animal.
senses.example: I rode my bike around the block.

senses.definition: A trip on a vehicle, animal, or amusement machine.
senses.example: We went for a ride on the merry-go-round.

senses.definition: Correct or suitable for what is needed.
senses.example: She found the right answer by counting the groups.

senses.definition: The side that is opposite the left.
senses.example: Turn to the right after the bridge.

senses.definition: Something that people are allowed to do or are entitled to have under a rule or law.
senses.example: We learned about the right to vote.

senses.definition: To set something upright again after it has tipped or fallen over.
senses.example: We helped right the empty flowerpot after it fell.

senses.definition: An angle that makes a square corner and measures ninety degrees.
senses.example: The sides of a sheet of paper meet at a right angle.

senses.definition: A natural solid material made of one or more minerals or other solid substances.
senses.example: We saw three different colors in the rock.

senses.definition: To move gently back and forth or from side to side.
senses.example: The small boat began to rock when a wave went past.

senses.definition: A kind of popular music often played with a strong beat, guitars, and drums.
senses.example: The drummer plays in a rock band.

senses.definition: A cell near the back of the eye that responds well to weak light.
senses.example: Rod cells help me see the ground in very dim light.

senses.definition: The turning of something around a center or an axis. The word can also mean one whole turn.
senses.example: Earth’s rotation gives us day and night.

senses.definition: An order in which people or things take turns so each has a chance.
senses.example: The coach wrote down the rotation for each position.

senses.definition: A machine part that spins, such as the blades on top of a helicopter.
senses.example: The helicopter’s rotor pushed air downward.

senses.definition: Changing a number to a nearby, simpler number, such as the closest ten.
senses.example: Rounding 48 to the nearest ten gives 50.

senses.definition: A device or program that passes packets toward other computer networks.
senses.example: A router can send a message from our home network toward the internet.

senses.definition: A movable part that helps turn the nose of a boat or an aircraft from side to side.
senses.example: The rudder can swing one way or the other at the back of the plane’s tail.

senses.definition: To move quickly on foot, taking quicker steps than when walking.
senses.example: I ran to the big tree and back.

senses.definition: To operate a machine or continue working.
senses.example: The fan can run all afternoon.

senses.definition: To manage the work of a group, activity, or place.
senses.example: The student council helped run the book fair.

senses.definition: An outing or exercise in which someone moves quickly on foot.
senses.example: We went for a run before breakfast.

senses.definition: A stem that creeps away from a parent plant and can make new plants along the way.
senses.example: The strawberry’s runner reached over the edge of the pot.

senses.definition: Water that flows off land or buildings instead of staying where it fell or soaking into the ground.
senses.example: Runoff followed the edge of the road into a drain.
